precepts.text: The Most High returns to His place until we acknowledge our offense and seek Him early in our affliction.
precepts.point: When the Most High is silent against us it is the same thing as Hosea: He withdraws and does not listen to our prayers until we seek His face.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Unto thee will I cry, O Lord my rock; be not silent to me: lest, if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.” When the Most High is silent against us, it is the same thing as Hosea: “I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face: in their affliction they will seek me early.”

He withdraws and returns to His place, and does not listen to our prayers, until we acknowledge our offense and seek His face. In our affliction we seek Him early. That is why David cries, be not silent to me, and lifts up his hands toward the holy oracle.

precepts.text: His words were smoother than butter but war was in his heart; this wicked is Esau.
precepts.point: Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch. But the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Draw me not away with the wicked, and with the workers of iniquity, which speak peace to their neighbours, but mischief is in their hearts.” Here is that wicked: “The words of his mouth were smoother than butter, but war was in his heart: his words were softer than oil, yet were they drawn swords.”

Words smoother than butter, but war in his heart; this wicked is Esau. Some wickedness is visible and clear, like homosexuality, but there is wickedness you will not pick up on as easily, peace in the mouth and mischief in the heart, and men are judged for it. David is giving clues about the different types of wicked that will be judged.

precepts.text: Esau's pride and desire to exalt himself as God brings the Most High's promise to bring him down.
precepts.point: Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch. But the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone.

note.label: Psalm 28: Be Not Silent To Me

precepts.why:
“Because they regard not the works of the Lord, nor the operation of his hands, he shall destroy them, and not build them up.” That is Esau. Esau does not regard the operations of the Most High; they want to be as God, above God, in their sciences and everything their hands touch.

“The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee, thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, whose habitation is high; that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground? Though thou exalt thyself as the eagle, and though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.” Esau's pride and desire to exalt himself as God brings the Most High's promise to bring him down.

And the wicked, whether Esau or our own people, will not be built back up once destroyed. When those bombs hit, they are gone. He gives them according to their deeds, and destroys them, and does not build them up.
